sourceOccurrences.label: Schur products, blocks and Ando comparison
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:2106.06400v3; Appendix A, Proposition A.4, Theorems A.5–A.6 and Lemmas A.7–A.8, printed pp. 30–33

sourceOccurrences.note: Gram matrices prove Schur positivity and tensor compression proves its norm bound. Completing the square proves the Schur complement under a uniform lower bound. Gram block factorizations prove the full semidefinite Ando statement without inverses. Source-inspected; not a compiled association or reviewed source correspondence.

sourceOccurrences.label: Invariant roots and the faithful trace
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:2106.06400v3; Appendix A, Lemma A.9, Proposition A.10 and Lemma A.11, printed pp. 34–35
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Detailed prose proof with explicit operator and limiting hypotheses
sourceOccurrences.note: Unitary conjugation preserves the unique positive square root, with norm exponent one half. Absolute convergence precedes signed mass transport. Transitivity proves faithfulness, and cyclicity proves positivity of the trace of a product. Source-inspected; not a compiled association or reviewed source correspondence.

sourceOccurrences.note: Monotone convergence of the expanded nonnegative diagrams extends IZAO to a common monotone approximation with finite susceptibility. Finite-path coupling and the existing sharpness argument supply the independent-percolation critical specialization, also when the threshold is infinite. Source-inspected; not a compiled association or reviewed source correspondence.

sourceOccurrences.label: Euclidean and hierarchical Fourier comparison
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:2106.06400v3, Section 2, equations (2.8)–(2.10) and the final hierarchical paragraph, printed pp. 14–15
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Fourier proof with the hierarchical compact product dual
sourceOccurrences.note: Finite-set character quadratic forms prove nonnegativity of the summable kernel transform. Character orthogonality gives the diagrams, Hölder gives A <= Delta squared, and convolution Cauchy–Schwarz gives B <= A. Counting measure on the discrete group and normalized Haar measure on the compact dual are distinct. The existing dual-group diagnosis stays provisional.
